description: I am a Computer Science student with a strong interest in space exploration, technology, software development, and problem-solving. I enjoy exploring innovative ideas and turning them into practical projects that combine creativity with technology. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, I am particularly interested in developing interactive educational experiences that make complex scientific and engineering concepts easier to understand.
summary:
Mission Control is an interactive C++-based Space Mission Design Game developed to make space mission planning more accessible, engaging, and educational. Players take on the role of a mission director and design missions to explore Earth, the Moon, or Mars. They select scientific instruments, spacecraft components, power systems, communication equipment, propulsion systems, and launch vehicles.

The game addresses the challenge by simulating real-world engineering trade-offs. Players must manage limited budgets, spacecraft mass, power consumption, communication capacity, and scientific requirements while making decisions that directly affect mission success. It includes a resource dashboard, engineering constraint checks, mission simulation, scoring system, and feedback explaining mission outcomes.

This project is important because it transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an interactive learning experience. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, experimentation, and scientific curiosity while helping students understand how different engineering decisions work together to achieve a successful space mission.
details:
What does the project do and how does it work?

Mission Control is an interactive, C++-based Space Mission Design Game that allows players to experience the process of planning and managing a space mission. Players take on the role of a mission director and choose between three mission types: Earth observation, Moon exploration, and Mars exploration. They then design their spacecraft by selecting scientific instruments, power systems, batteries, communication equipment, propulsion systems, and launch vehicles.

The game uses simplified engineering calculations to evaluate the player's choices. It checks important constraints such as spacecraft mass, available budget, power requirements, communication capacity, and propulsion capability. After the design is completed, the game simulates the mission and provides a score and feedback explaining its outcome.

What benefits does it have?

The project makes basic aerospace engineering concepts easier to understand through interactive decision-making. Instead of simply reading about spacecraft design, players can experiment with different components, compare trade-offs, manage limited resources, and learn how engineering decisions affect mission success.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to encourage interest in space exploration, science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). We hope to make space mission planning more accessible to students and beginners while developing their critical thinking, creativity, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

The project was developed using:

  • Programming language: C++
  • Language standard: C++11
  • Development approach: Object-oriented programming, functions, conditional statements, loops, and simplified engineering calculations.
  • Interface: Text-based, interactive console interface.
  • Hardware: A standard computer for development and running the program.

No specialized aerospace hardware or external simulation equipment was required.

How is the project creative?

Mission Control transforms the complex process of spacecraft design into an interactive educational game. Its creative aspect lies in allowing players to make their own mission-planning decisions and experience the consequences of those decisions. Different combinations of spacecraft components and launch vehicles can produce different outcomes, encouraging experimentation and strategic thinking.

What factors did the team consider?

The project was designed around several important factors:

  • Mission objectives: Different requirements for Earth, Moon, and Mars missions.
  • Budget: Keeping the mission within financial limits.
  • Mass constraints: Ensuring the spacecraft does not exceed launch capacity.
  • Power management: Matching available power with spacecraft requirements.
  • Communication: Considering the spacecraft's ability to transmit scientific data.
  • Propulsion: Evaluating whether the selected propulsion system and launch vehicle meet simplified mission requirements.
  • Scientific value: Selecting instruments that contribute to the mission's objectives.
  • Educational accessibility: Keeping the game understandable and engaging for beginners.

Ultimately, Mission Control aims to demonstrate that successful space exploration requires careful planning, resource management, scientific knowledge, and engineering decisions working together.
